title: PRD — phased retirement of v0 model aliases with adaptive compatibility shim and rollback criteria
creator: Marina Gomez
description: This PRD defines the plan to retire legacy v0 model aliases (e.g., model: v0-*) that currently increase routing complexity, block kernel/quantization upgrades, and confuse clients. We will provide an adaptive compatibility shim and SDK warnings to minimize breakage, coordinate a staged cutover, and define clear acceptance and rollback gates.
background: Historically we exposed 'v0' model aliases to maintain backwards compatibility for early adopters. Over time these aliases have diverged from the canonical model naming used in the runtime and model catalog, increasing routing permutations and hampering performance optimizations (kernel selection, quantization profiles). Several infra changes (runtime-2.0 kernels, aliasless model promotion) require a consolidated naming model to simplify routing and support automated fallbacks.
goals: Remove long-lived v0 model aliases from public API surface with minimal client disruption
Ship an adaptive compatibility shim that translates v0 alias calls to canonical model versions with telemetry and rate-limited fallback
Provide SDK and CLI warnings and automated migration helpers for major client languages
Define deterministic acceptance criteria (latency, error rate, customer opt-in) and rollback gates
non_goals: Rewriting customer prompts or application logic beyond what automated adapters can safely do
Forcing customers to upgrade models immediately; we will not remove model content but retire alias indirection
Concurrent major changes to billing models or reserved capacity semantics
scope_included: Public REST endpoints that accept model aliases (v0-*)
SDK warnings and migration helpers for JavaScript, Python, and Go
Compatibility shim hosted in control plane with configurable TTL and rate limits
Telemetry and dashboards (per-alias usage, error trends, migration progress)
scope_excluded: Private customer-managed on-prem runtimes (they get a separate advisory)
Deep model compatibility edits (e.g., automating prompt reformulation)
Manual migration support beyond providing automated tooling and step-by-step guides
migration_strategy: Three-pronged strategy: 1) Provide a compatibility shim in the control plane that maps v0 aliases to a pinned canonical model version; the shim will attach a deprecation header and emit telemetry. 2) Ship SDK updates (minor versions) that surface a 'deprecated alias' warning and supply a one-line replacement command. 3) Coordinate phased removal by customer cohorts: internal, early adopters (opt-in), then gradual enforcement with rate limits and finally alias removal after a 90-day warning window.
rollout_phases: Phase 0 (canary, 2 weeks): Deploy shim for internal traffic and Redwood-managed test customers; verify latency and correctness against golden prompts
Phase 1 (public opt-in, 4 weeks): Enable shim for customers who opt in via Console toggle; publish SDKs and migration docs; collect migration telemetry
Phase 2 (soft deprecation, 8 weeks): Emit deprecation responses by default; apply gentle rate limits to alias TTL translations for new sessions; continue support for pinned sessions
Phase 3 (enforcement, 4 weeks): Stop new alias-to-canonical mappings for non-migrated clients; keep short-term fallbacks for in-flight sessions and provide emergency on-call support
Phase 4 (removal): Complete alias removal from routing table after 90 days notice and migration completion metrics met
acceptance_criteria: <1% increase in p95 latency for requests routed through shim during Phase 0
No more than 0.1% increase in 5xx errors attributable to alias routing across Phase 1
>= 85% of active v0 alias traffic either migrated or opted in to shim within 8 weeks of public opt-in
SDKs and Console migration docs published and linked; at least two major client libraries show successful auto-migration in integration tests
Runbooks and rollback playbook validated with a simulated failure scenario and on-call drills
monitoring_and_telemetry: Per-alias request volume and error rates (dashboard)
Migration funnel: warning impressions, SDK upgrades, Console toggles, successful canonical calls
End-to-end latency histograms for shim and direct routes
Customer-reported incidents tagged with alias ID and steering metadata
rollback_and_risk_mitigation: Shim is feature-flagged and can be globally disabled within 5 minutes
Maintain a read-only fallback that routes to last-known-good canonical mapping for critical customers
Pre-coordinate support rotations and escalation paths with SRE/Support
Threshold-based abort: if alias-related 5xx exceeds 0.5% or p95 latency increases >15% during any phase, pause rollout and revert shim changes
notes: We will offer a 'migration concierge' for top 10 revenue customers. Legal/compliance to review communication for regulated customers. Product marketing will draft deprecation emails and Console banners. Track cost impact of shim (control plane compute) and evaluate chargeback if significant.
